src/business/entities/Appointment.ts: `@Column() id: string;` maps a field to a database column (infrastructure/persistence responsibility).
Domain methods endsAt(), overlaps(), cancel(now) with the two-hour cancellation rule are appropriate for the domain layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The Appointment entity sits in the business (domain) layer. Its domain behaviour fits that layer: endsAt, overlaps, and cancel with its two-hour cancellation rule. However, the class also carries persistence-mapping responsibility. It is decorated with TypeORM's @Entity() and its id field with @Column(), which tie the domain entity to an ORM schema mapping. That is infrastructure (persistence) logic placed in a domain file. The import of typeorm itself is an import-direction concern and out of scope. The decorators, though, give the class an ORM-mapping role, and that role belongs to the persistence layer.
